title: The Morning Digest: November 9, 2026
dek: Oil opened the week softer and choppy in Asia, Brent Jan27 at $97.67 and WTI Dec26 at $90.51 on the latest Reuters snapshot (1134 GMT) against Friday settles of $98.32 and $90.83 (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 6). UKMTO confirmed a tanker fire with the crew evacuated northwest of Khasab and a second outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 7; the mechanism behind both is unconfirmed and the IRGC mine claim remains a claim. The Baltic Week 45 weekly (week ending Nov 6) shows TD9 down from WS710 to WS397 and TD25 down from about WS707 to WS399, while the Brent to WTI spread narrowed to $7.49 at Friday's settle. On the current balance build, November supply runs about 192 kb/d above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound and December about 216 kb/d above, with the overflow going to tank. December WCS is -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots. The validated diesel crack is $91.19.

Nov 8, 2026 for Nov 7 incidents (a tanker caught fire at 1920 UTC about 8 nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman, and the crew was evacuated, cause not stated; a second outbound tanker was struck by an unknown projectile at 2020 UTC while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, all crew safe, no environmental impact reported); JMIC severe threat assessment retained, about 162 vessels anchored around Fujairah and Khor Fakkan on Nov 8

Nov 7, 2026 (US forces disabled the St. Kitts-flagged bulk carrier M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman with precision munitions at its stern after repeated warnings; cumulative tally since the blockade resumed in July: 147 vessels redirected, five merchant ships disabled; a new Task Force Iron Gate was announced to extend interdiction to land borders and the Caspian); IRGC via Xinhua and Fars, Nov 7-9, 2026 (two tankers claimed on naval mines and a third tanker explosion reported; no vessel named; Reuters unable to confirm the mine strikes; maritime press notes the mechanism of the reported explosions, mines, missiles or drones, is unclear)

Nov 7, 2026, and Reuters, Nov 8-9, 2026 (the Qatari two-day bridge proposal: day one, the US lifts the naval blockade and releases part of about $8 billion in frozen assets while Iran admits IAEA inspectors to its bombed nuclear sites; day two, the strait reopens through the route negotiated with Oman and nuclear talks resume; Tehran submitted its own nuclear proposal through Doha conditional on sanctions relief, unfreezing funds and reparations, and says it awaits Washington's answer; Qatar denies the talks have failed; the US president meets the Qatari prime minister on Nov 9 at 12:00 p.m. ET)
